title: Optimize walkthrough — batching & prefix/KV cache cost model (Orchid Tech)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Orchid Tech through Redwood Optimize recommendations focusing on request batching and prefix/KV cache strategies. Diego demoed the Console cost model spreadsheet and showed simulated throughput/costs. Customer asked about cold-starts, cache invalidation, data residency, and SLA behavior. Agreed to run a 2-week POC with sample traffic and shared benchmark template and security pack.
action_items: Samira to send annotated cost spreadsheet and raw CSV model by 2025-04-11
Diego to run a 2-hour synthetic benchmark on Redwood hosted matching Orchid token distribution and share logs by 2025-04-14
Liam to provide 7-day sample traffic traces and example prompt set by 2025-04-12
Tom to circulate security questionnaire answers and ask for SOC2 report via support link by 2025-04-13
next_steps: Share Optimize config suggestion JSON + recommended batch_size and prefix TTLs
Provide Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta sheet and latency SLO comparison
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-04-09 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Huang (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Orchid ML), Liam O'Connor (Orchid Platform), Tom Adler (Orchid CISO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through Optimize recommendations; focused on batching and prefix/KV cache tradeoffs. Customer concerned about cache invalidation, PII leakage, and bursty traffic cost. Action items and POC agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Samira, AE on Redwood Inference, and Diego is our SE who owns the Optimize tooling.
[00:22] Maya: Hi, I'm Maya. We're trying to get cost down on our chat summarization pipeline without spiking latency.
[00:30] Diego: Great, that's exactly what Optimize targets. Today we'll show Console views, the cost model, and some specific prefix / K-V cache recommendations. Sorry spelling -- sometimes the auto transcript writes K-V cash.
[00:45] Liam: Quick ask — our workload is bursty, lots of short prompts ~70 tokens, sometimes longer context 1.2k tokens. We need 95th percentile latencies <200ms.
[01:05] Diego: Understood. Two levers: batching (reduce per-token kernel overhead) and prefix/KV caching (avoid re-attending to repeated system instructions or persona). We'll show samples.
[01:28] Samira: We'll also show the cost model. Important note: numbers are simulation, we'll calibrate during POC.
[01:40] Tom: From security side, if you're doing prefix caching, how is the cached data encrypted and who owns the keys?
[01:52] Diego: Good question. For Redwood hosted we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and Dedicated. In Console you can toggle encryption at rest flags; still, transcript: sometimes speaks S-O-C 2 instead of SOC2.
[02:15] Maya: Can batching hurt latency on single-user interactive flows?
[02:30] Diego: Yes, if you only do time-window batching. Optimize suggests adaptive batching: do small immediate batches for interactive and larger batching for background jobs. For your short prompts we'd recommend batch_size=8 with max_wait_ms=50 for interactive endpoints. For background summarizers batch_size=64 with max_wait_ms=200.
[03:05] Maya: Do you have numbers? We need to justify to finance.
[03:12] Samira: Yup — here's a sample from the cost sheet: baseline single-request (no batching, no cache) for a 512-token call ~ $0.018 per call. With batching to 8 and prefix cache hit-rate 30% you drop to ~ $0.006 per call equivalent. Those numbers are estimates — Diego will run your sample distribution to tune.
[03:40] Liam: That seems big. How do you compute cache hit-rate?
[03:48] Diego: We use recent prefix usage stats: for PLA demos we saw 25-40% prefix reuse in customer corpora. For you, short prompts with common system messages should yield 30-50%. We'll compute a simulated hit-rate from your 7-day sample.
[04:10] Maya: What about cache invalidation if prompts change?
[04:18] Diego: Prefix cache keys are fingerprinted hashes of the prefix tokens+model+version. Invalidate by TTL or by key purge via API. In practice we advise a 6-24 hour TTL depending on churn; for high-change you can use shorter TTLs. If you have PII in prefix, we recommend not caching that or stripping before caching.
[04:45] Tom: That PII bit — do you support token scrubbing or client-side redaction in the runtime?
[04:53] Diego: We have hooks in ingest to run redaction; can be customer-side or via a Redwood pipeline if you opt in. For Private deployments you keep all data on-prem.
[05:10] [Small crosstalk]
[05:22] Samira: Diego, can you share the Console screen and the Optimize cost tab?
[05:30] Diego: Sure. (screen share) Here is the cost model CSV. Column A is scenario, B is average tokens, C is batch size, D is prefix hit, E is modeled cost per 1k requests. Note sometimes the Console label shows 'pre-fix cache' broken with a hyphen in the UI.
[06:05] Diego: Example scenario: interactive chat, avg tokens 140, batch_size 8, prefix_hit 35% -> modeled cost per 1k reqs: $4.2. Unbatched same workload -> $12.8 per 1k. So roughly 3x improvement.
[06:30] Maya: What about latency tail when batching? If we batch to 8 there's a queueing delay.
[06:38] Diego: Yes — the model's throughput also matters. For small GPT-style models we measured ~300 tokens/sec on our GPU config; queuing adds (batch_size-1)*arrival_interarrival_time average. Optimize suggests patient/urgent route config: urgent requests skip batching or use a smaller micro-batch.
[06:58] Liam: Could we do per-customer routing? e.g., priority users go to low-latency pool, others to batched pool?
[07:08] Samira: Absolutely. Smart routing is supported via per-route policies in Console. We'll include a recommended routing map in the POC docs.
[07:25] Diego: Also important: KV cache vs prefix cache difference. Prefix cache stores initial attention prefixes and is great for repeating system prompts. KV cache is the attention key-value cache for long-decoding sequences and is used to avoid recomputing past contexts, but it doesn't reduce compute for the current request unless you reuse prefixes across requests.
[07:52] Maya: So KV cache helps with long conversations but not cross-session reuse?
[07:58] Diego: Correct — KV cache is per-session and persists in fast memory during a session. If you want cross-session reuse, that's prefix caching or a precomputed embedding-based rerank.
[08:15] Tom: Any risks around cache poisoning?
[08:21] Diego: We fingerprint keys and enforce ACLs. For Hosted we store cache entries in encrypted stores; Dedicated gives you more isolation. We'll include the security note in the file.
[08:40] [15-second pause]
[08:55] Maya: Walk me through an end-to-end POC we could run.
[09:02] Samira: Plan idea: 2-week POC, deploy a mirrored endpoint in Redwood hosted, run your 7-day traffic replay with 50% real-time interactive traffic and 50% background summarizers. We'll measure cost/latency with default settings, then apply Optimize recommendations (batching + prefix TTL) and compare. Rancho? sorry, transcript says Rancho sometimes for benchmarking.
[09:35] Diego: We'll collect metrics: cost per 1k, p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit-rate, and token throughput. We'll share the raw logs and a cleaned dashboard.
[09:52] Liam: What about Dedicated? If we later move to Dedicated, does the same batching config translate?
[10:00] Diego: Yes — the serving runtime behaves the same; kernel selection may differ slightly if you pick different GPU types. We'll show the Dedicated cost delta in the spreadsheet. Usually Dedicated reduces per-token price at higher commits but requires capacity planning.
[10:18] Maya: Any gotchas with quantized models? We use 4-bit quant in some runs.
[10:25] Diego: Quantization generally reduces GPU memory and can increase throughput. Optimize will recommend quantization profiles by workload — but for chat-style low-latency we sometimes avoid aggressive quant to avoid output variance. We'll flag model quality in the report.
[10:45] Tom: Audit logs and retention? We need 13 months for compliance.
[10:51] Samira: We can configure extended retention as an add-on for Private/Dedicated. Hosted has default retention windows but enterprise plans can extend. We'll attach the compliance pack.
[11:10] Diego: Back to cost math briefly — in the sheet we show per-token compute cost + memory overhead amortized across batch. For example, an unbatched 512-token call had compute time X and per-call scheduling overhead Y; batching reduces scheduling overhead per-token. The modeled savings assume a cache hit avoids the initial prefix recompute which is ~30% of cost in our microbenchmarks.
[11:45] Maya: Can you share the microbenchmark scripts? We want to run locally to validate.
[11:52] Diego: Yes, we'll share a small harness. It's in the repo link in the notes. Note: sometimes script names in the transcript show as bench_run_v1 and bench_run-v1 interchangeably.
[12:10] [Diego screenshares a live benchmark run — partial transcript]
[12:15] Diego: This run simulates your mix: 60% short prompts 70 tokens, 40% long contexts 1.2k. Without cache, QPS is 120 and avg latency 170ms; with batching and prefix cache hit at 33%, QPS improves to 330 and avg latency drops to 95ms on this host. Again these are synthetic.
[13:00] Maya: Those numbers look promising. What's the expected infra cost difference?
[13:06] Samira: In the cost sheet we estimated monthly inference spend would go from approx $18k -> $6.2k for similar volume after Optimize. Diego will refine with your actual traces.
[13:28] Liam: Is there a way to see the cache hit breaking down by endpoint?
[13:35] Diego: Yes — Console shows per-route cache metrics and you can drill to token-level histograms. We'll point to the exact dashboard.
[13:50] Tom: Any data residency issues with caching? If we cache prefixes that contain EU-personal data and our region is US, can we force cache region?
[14:00] Diego: Yes — with region pinning and Private you can keep caches in-region. For Hosted, we can pin region and follow data residency controls. We'll capture this in the security doc.
[14:20] Maya: Let's talk success criteria for the POC — what should we aim for?
[14:28] Samira: Suggested criteria: 2x cost reduction or better on production-like workload, p95 < 200ms for interactive routes, cache hit-rate >25% for targeted endpoints, and no functional regressions on 1000 golden prompts.
[14:47] Maya: Sounds good. Finance will likely push for guaranteed numbers.
[14:52] Samira: We'll be careful in language — we won't guarantee until we run your traffic. But we can commit to run the bench and share deterministic results.
[15:05] [Diego shares a sample Optimize config JSON]
[15:12] Diego: Example snippet: route: 'chat-interactive' -> batch_size 8, max_wait_ms 50, prefix_ttl_hours 12, prefix_backfill false. For summarizer: batch_size 64, max_wait_ms 200, prefix_ttl_hours 24, prefix_backfill true.
[15:42] Maya: What's prefix_backfill?
[15:46] Diego: It's a background job that precomputes prefix entries for frequent prompts so the first user doesn't hit cold-start. It uses additional compute to prefill useful cache entries.
[16:10] Liam: Does prefill cost more? Is it worth it?
[16:16] Diego: It adds some background cost, but for high-frequency prefixes it pays off quickly by reducing first-call cost and improving latency. We'll simulate ROI in the spreadsheet.
[16:35] Maya: Any notes about request signing or auth for cache purge APIs?
[16:40] Samira: All admin APIs require API keys with RBAC and we recommend using SAML-based SCIM provisioning for users.
[16:52] Tom: I'd like the SOC2 and pen-test summary before we kick off.
[16:58] Samira: We'll attach SOC2 and a redacted pen-test summary to the folder.
[17:10] Maya: Ok, let's confirm POC dates.
[17:15] Samira: Tentative kickoff week of 2025-04-21, run two weeks, finish by 2025-05-05.
[17:25] Liam: I'll get traffic traces by 2025-04-12.
[17:30] Samira: Great. We'll also send an annotated cost spreadsheet and the bench harness.
[17:40] Tom: Couple quick clarifying questions on RBAC later via email.
[17:45] Samira: Perfect. Any final concerns?
[17:50] Maya: None on this call. Thanks both.
[17:55] Samira: Thanks everyone. Recap: Samira send sheet, Diego run synthetic, Liam provide traces, Tom provide security answers. We'll schedule POC kickoff.
[18:10] [meeting ends, brief hold music]

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-hearings and UI label typos as typical from auto transcript. References to spreadsheets and repo links were promised; links will be shared in meeting notes.
